- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.11) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.22) or recent prices are falling — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) by forecasting further gains — apply lagged correction: reduce forecast by 5-10% after a spike.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.06–0.17), model often overestimates — apply mean reversion: cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) — reduce first 5 forecasts by 2–5% to align with observed lag.
- If sentiment is strongly negative and prices are trending down, model often ignores the trend — force downward adjustment by 3–5% per negative sentiment unit below 0.0.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals without recent sentiment confirmation — if sentiment flips from +0.17 to -0.22, reduce forecast by 5–10% immediately.
